reader.requirement: At --std 85 a CLOSE, OPEN, READ, REWRITE or WRITE on a sequential file that executes successfully must set its I-O status to a Successful Completion value (00, or 04 / 05 / 07 in their listed cases) and must not execute a USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure, for fixed and RECORD VARYING records and every 1985 open mode and CLOSE phrase.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility: no file-sharing facility at 85 (records buffered while the connector is alone; siblings released at OPEN); the success status is unchanged
DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 85 CLOSE WITH LOCK locks the physical file, from 2002 the connector; the CLOSE itself reports 00 at both

reader.edition-search: grep for DialectBehavior.|DialectLevel|CobolVersion in src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO: the status constants and the success-family tests (status[0] == '0') are edition-free; the two hits above touch sharing and the lock, not the success values.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the Successful Completion values themselves; the edition-dependent arms change what a later OPEN sees after CLOSE WITH LOCK and how connectors share, not the status of the successful statement
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf18_01 covers 00 for OPEN (OUTPUT, EXTEND, I-O, INPUT), WRITE, READ, REWRITE and CLOSE and no USE on success; not exercised: 05 for an absent OPTIONAL file (INPUT and EXTEND, created), 07 for CLOSE WITH NO REWIND, OPEN WITH NO REWIND and CLOSE REEL on disk, 04 for a short record, RECORD VARYING records, CLOSE WITH LOCK, and the USE procedure staying silent for 04/05/07

probes.printed: E1 OPEN-INPUT-OPTIONAL-ABSENT 05 USES 0; E2 CLOSE 00; E3 OPEN-EXTEND-OPTIONAL-ABSENT 05; E4 WRITE 00; E5 CLOSE-NO-REWIND 07; E6 OPEN-NO-REWIND 07; E7 READ 00 WXYZ; E8 CLOSE-REEL 07; E9 CLOSE 00; A6 CLOSE-LOCK 00 USES 0
probes.expected: 05 for an absent optional file (EXTEND creates it, the later READ finds WXYZ), 07 for a NO REWIND / REEL phrase on a non-reel medium, 00 otherwise, and no USE procedure for any of them (§1985:VII.1.3.5 Successful Completion a-d)

probes.printed: A1 WRITE3 00; A2 WRITE10 00; A3 CLOSE 00; A4 READ 00 03 ABC; A5 READ 00 10 0123456789
probes.expected: RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON records of 3 and 10 written and read with 00, the depending item set by READ
a failed OPEN of a non-optional absent file is not successful: 35, the USE procedure runs once, then the next statement

probes.printed: L1 00 AAAA USES 0; L2 04 USES 0; USE RAN 10; L3 10 USES 1
probes.expected: a READ of a 2-byte remainder of a 4-character fixed file is 04 (successful, no USE); the next READ is at end 10 with no AT END phrase, so USE runs

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5 GR1  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: The connectors return the success-family constants and the registry and USE machinery treat a status beginning 0 as successful at every edition; every Successful Completion case 1985 lists printed its value with the USE procedure silent, and a failed OPEN ran it. A side probe (ios2.cob, a varying file read through a 4-character FD) read raw 4-byte chunks with 00, which is the implementor's physical-format latitude, not a finding.

refuter.evidence: rios.cob (rios-002): OPEN I-O of an absent OPTIONAL file, a case the reader did not try -> 05, no USE; the next READ -> 10 at end; rios2.cob: after OPEN I-O of absent OPTIONAL NOFILE3 and CLOSE, a non-optional SELECT of the same name opens INPUT with 00, so the 1985 'If the open mode is I-O or extend, the file has been created' holds. REWRITE after OPEN I-O -> 00; CLOSE REEL FOR REMOVAL, CLOSE UNIT, CLOSE REEL, CLOSE UNIT FOR REMOVAL on disk -> 07 each, the file still open after each (a later plain CLOSE -> 00); CLOSE WITH NO REWIND and OPEN INPUT WITH NO REWIND -> 07; the USE procedure counter stayed 0 through every success value. Class c: CLOSE F1 FOR REMOVAL without REEL/UNIT is refused (COBOL2269), as the 1985 CLOSE format allows FOR REMOVAL only after REEL/UNIT. The runtime IO DialectBehavior grep (FileConnector#SharingFacilityInEffect, FileRegistry#CloseWithLock, the indexed and relative arms) shows no other site on the sequential success path. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.1c; OK §1985:VII.4.2.1 the text is in the clause.
